claims.text: No lab or imaging test diagnoses schizophrenia.
claims.quote: No definitive laboratory or imaging test for schizophrenia exists.

claims.text: Rule out medical and substance causes with history, exam, labs and neuroimaging.
claims.quote: Psychosis due to other medical disorders or to substance use disorders must be ruled out by history and examination that includes laboratory tests and neuroimaging

claims.text: Screening labs for new or markedly changed symptoms: CBC; electrolytes with calcium and magnesium, BUN, creatinine; ESR or CRP; HIV; urinalysis.
claims.quote: Complete blood count Electrolyte levels (including calcium and magnesium), blood urea nitrogen, and creatinine Erythrocyte sedimentation rate or C-reactive protein HIV testing Urinalysis

claims.text: Head CT for new-onset symptoms, delirium, headache, recent trauma or focal neurologic findings.
claims.quote: Head CT: Patients with new-onset psychiatric symptoms or with delirium, headache, history of recent physical trauma, or focal neurologic findings (eg, weakness of an extremity)

claims.text: Lumbar puncture with meningeal signs, or a normal head CT plus fever, headache or delirium.
claims.quote: Lumbar puncture : Patients with meningeal signs or with normal head CT findings plus fever, headache, or delirium

claims.text: Thyroid function tests on lithium, with thyroid signs, or over 40 with new symptoms.
claims.quote: Thyroid function tests: Patients taking lithium , those with symptoms or signs of thyroid disease, and those > 40 years with new-onset psychiatric symptoms (particularly females or patients with a family history of thyroid disease)

claims.text: Toxicology screen (urine drug screen, blood alcohol) with recent substance use or signs of it.
claims.quote: Toxicology screening (eg, urine drug screen, blood alcohol level) is done if the patient has a recent history of substance use disorder or physical signs suggesting intoxication or recent substance use (eg, needle marks).

claims.text: Amphetamine psychosis can't be reliably told apart from primary psychosis; full resolution after stopping use points to the drug.
claims.quote: Amphetamine -induced paranoia or psychosis are not reliably distinguishable from primary psychiatric disorders. However, if symptoms and signs of autonomic nervous system dysregulation are present and/or psychosis resolves completely with cessation of amphetamine use, this suggests the etiology is amphetamine use than a primary psychiatric disorder.
